stories.headline: Ukraine's largest barrage of the war sets Moscow's main refinery ablaze as Russia votes

key_facts.fact: Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones plus missiles at Russia overnight into Sept. 20; Russia's Defense Ministry said it shot down 1,110 drones across Russia, Crimea and the Black Sea, while Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin called it the 'largest ever' drone attack on the capital and said 450 were destroyed en route to Moscow.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia's Ministry of Defense said Sunday that its forces shot down a total of 1,110 Ukrainian drones across Russia... Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said that 450 drones had been destroyed en route to the Russian capital, and that the attack had damaged the Moscow Oil Refinery and a residential building.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's General Staff said long-range strikes hit the AVT-6 primary crude processing unit, an integrated refining unit and an isomerization unit at the Gazprom Neft Moscow Oil Refinery in Kapotnya, about 15 km from the Kremlin; SBU Alpha drones flew over 500 km to reach it.
key_facts.excerpt: According to the General Staff, long-range strikes hit the AVT-6 primary crude processing unit, an integrated oil refining unit, and an isomerization unit, sparking a large fire across the plant. Long-range Alpha drones from the SBU flew over 500 kilometers to breach Russian air defenses and strike the facility.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said the operation used a mix of Ukrainian-made systems including FP-1, RZ-100, MICH-2000, Palianytsia, Vendetta, Liutyi, Bars, Flamingo and the new Pelican missile, and also hit an industrial facility in Russia's Voronezh region.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelensky stated that Ukrainian forces deployed various long-range strike systems, including FP-1, RZ-100, MICH-2000, Palianytsia, Vendetta, Liutyi, Bars, Flamingo, Sichnevyi, and Pelican. Ukrainian forces also hit an industrial facility in Russia's Voronezh region.

key_facts.fact: The strikes landed on the final day of Russia's first wartime State Duma election, held Sept. 18-20, from which the antiwar Yabloko party was disqualified in August; Russia's defence ministry vowed to 'continue and intensify' precision strikes on military facilities in Kyiv.
key_facts.excerpt: Yabloko, a liberal party that would have been the only party on the ballot calling for an end to the war on Ukraine, was disqualified in August on what its leaders said were 'absurd' grounds.

key_facts.fact: Russian drones killed a woman and three children in the Kyiv region over the weekend, and Ukraine's military reported 138 Russian attack drones striking 17 locations nationwide on Sept. 20.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's military reported 138 Russian attack drones striking at 17 locations nationwide, and authorities said four people were killed in the Kyiv region, including three children, one of them four years old.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said on Sept. 20 that he spoke with Trump by phone and agreed to meet in New York, expected Tuesday on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly; Axios reported Trump repeatedly urged him to stop striking Russian refineries because they are pushing up global diesel prices.
key_facts.excerpt: "Axios: A source familiar with the Trump-Zelensky call told Axios that Trump repeatedly urged Zelensky to stop Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries, arguing they were pushing up global diesel prices. 'The word diesel came up many times during the call,' source said."

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps said it retook another 40 square kilometers near Lyman in northern Donetsk region under Operation Vivaldi.
key_facts.excerpt: Brig. Gen. Andrii Biletskyi, commander of the 3rd Army Corps, said troops had reclaimed another 40 square kilometers, about 15 square miles, near Lyman in northern Donetsk during Operation Vivaldi.

stories.headline: Houthis hit Riyadh and Aramco's Yanbu hub as Saudi capital sounds first air-raid alert of the war

key_facts.fact: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said on Sept. 19 that Yemen's armed forces ran two operations with 'a large number of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones' — one against 'sensitive sites' in Riyadh and one against Aramco facilities in Yanbu.
key_facts.excerpt: "In response to the Saudi enemy's criminal attempts to target the capital Sana'a... the Yemeni Armed Forces carried out two successful military operations using a large number of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones," Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said... "The first targeted sensitive sites in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, and the second targeted Aramco facilities in Yanbu."

key_facts.fact: An AFP journalist saw firefighters extinguishing a blaze on a fuel tank bearing the Aramco logo at a depot near Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport; FlightRadar24 briefly listed the airport at its maximum disruption index.
key_facts.excerpt: Firefighters extinguished a blaze on a fuel tank with the logo of the Saudi oil giant Aramco at a fuel depot near the airport, an AFP journalist saw... Tracking website FlightRadar24 reported "major problems" at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, listing it for a while under its maximum disruption index.

key_facts.fact: Saudi civil defence sent phone alerts before 3:00 am warning residents of Riyadh and Al-Kharj that 'the area is under a hostile aerial threat' — the first such alert in the capital since the escalation with the Houthis began in July.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi civil defence sent the alerts by phone overnight for potential danger of aerial attacks in Riyadh and the city of Al-Kharj east of the capital, before issuing an all-clear on Saturday morning... these were the first since the escalation began with the Houthis in July.

key_facts.fact: The Saudi-led coalition said late Saturday that air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired at Riyadh and thwarted attempts on Yanbu, Taif, Bish and Farasan; spokesman Major-General Turki al-Maliki said the Houthis had also tried to hit civilians and civilian infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: "The Houthis also attempted to target civilians and civilian infrastructure in Bisha, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu," coalition forces spokesman Major-General Turki al-Maliki wrote on X on Saturday, adding that the attacks were thwarted by the Gulf monarchy's air defences.

key_facts.fact: The US State Department warned the Saudi-Houthi conflict 'has the potential to escalate rapidly' and told Americans outside the region to 'seriously reconsider travel to and through the region'.
key_facts.excerpt: "This military conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly," the US State Department warned, adding that American citizens outside the Middle East should "seriously reconsider travel to and through the region".

key_facts.fact: The Houthis, who seized Yemen's entire Red Sea coast this month, have attacked Saudi Arabia since declaring a naval blockade in July, putting at risk the main alternative Red Sea export route for Gulf crude while Hormuz stays blockaded.
key_facts.excerpt: The attacks have targeted Saudi cities, energy infrastructure and shipping, creating new threats to global oil supplies and putting at risk the main alternative Red Sea route for Gulf exports, while traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains blockaded. The Iran-aligned group... seized Yemen's entire Red Sea coast in a lightning advance this month.

key_facts.fact: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan condemned the attacks and said Saudi Arabia should be 'kept out' of the US-Iran conflict, adding Turkey was ready to help under the trilateral defence pact.
key_facts.excerpt: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan condemned the reported attacks on Saudi territory and oil infrastructure, saying the kingdom should be "kept out" of the broader conflict between Iran and the United States.

stories.headline: Iran sends the US seven conditions via Qatar and says Hormuz stays shut until they are met

key_facts.fact: Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei told Al Jazeera on Saturday, Sept. 19, that Tehran had conveyed its conditions to Washington through Qatari mediators, including an end to the war on all fronts including Lebanon, release of billions in frozen funds, an end to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports and an end to all US attacks on Iranian territory.
key_facts.excerpt: In an exclusive interview with Al Jazeera on Saturday, Rezaei said that Tehran has conveyed its conditions to the US via Qatari mediators... An end to the war on all fronts, including, in particular, Lebanon. The release of its frozen funds that run into billions of US dollars. An end to the naval blockade on Iranian ports.

key_facts.fact: Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf told the Iranian parliament on Sunday, Sept. 20, that there would be 'no opening' of the Strait of Hormuz until the seven conditions are met, arguing Iran must 'both fight and negotiate'.
key_facts.excerpt: Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf... said on Sunday (September 20, 2026) that the Strait of Hormuz would not be reopened until Iran's seven conditions were met, adding that Tehran must pursue both military action and negotiations.

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said on Sept. 20 that its forces had redirected 109 commercial vessels 'to ensure total compliance' in the waterway.
key_facts.excerpt: "CENTCOM forces have redirected 109 commercial vessels to ensure total compliance," CENTCOM said in a post on X.

key_facts.fact: A Joint Maritime Information Center update published Sunday recorded four tankers hit or approached near the Strait in the past week — MT TREND and an unnamed tanker on Sept. 17, STL STEADFAST and another on Sept. 18.
key_facts.excerpt: Two cases were recorded on September 17, involving MT TREND and an unnamed tanker, followed by two more on September 18 involving STL STEADFAST and another unnamed tanker.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya joint military command said Sunday it had information Washington was preparing to resume action against Iran, and warned regional states supporting an American attack would be treated as parties to the conflict.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya joint military command said it had received information that Washington, with approval from some regional countries, was preparing at a meeting in Europe to resume action against Iran. It also warned that regional states supporting an American attack would be treated as participants.

key_facts.fact: Iranian oil exports have fallen from roughly 2 million barrels a day before the war to about 220,000-255,000 barrels a day in August under the US blockade, and the conflict is now in its seventh month since US and Israeli strikes began on Feb. 28.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian oil exports have reportedly fallen from around 2 million barrels per day before the war to approximately 220,000–255,000 barrels per day in August... The conflict continues more than six months after US and Israeli strikes on Iran began on February 28.

key_facts.fact: Pakistan sent Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi to Tehran on Sunday as a second mediator, and Trump is due to discuss the war with leaders of six Gulf states in New York this week.
key_facts.excerpt: Pakistan, another key intermediary, is sending Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi to Tehran on Sunday... He is due to discuss the war with leaders of six Persian Gulf states in New York next week.

stories.headline: Beijing confirms Xi's Sept. 23-25 state visit as Bessent and He Lifeng negotiate in New York

key_facts.fact: China's foreign ministry announced on Monday, Sept. 21, that Xi Jinping will visit Washington from Sept. 23 to 25 at Trump's invitation, calling the reciprocal visits within six months a 'milestone of historic significance'.
key_facts.excerpt: Xi will visit the US for three days at the invitation of Trump, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun announced at a media briefing here on Monday. "The reciprocal visits by the two heads of state within a span of six months will mark a milestone of historic significance," he said.

key_facts.fact: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, USTR Jamieson Greer and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng met all day Sunday, Sept. 20, at JPMorgan Chase's Manhattan headquarters to prepare the summit, covering the trade truce that expires Nov. 10, rare-earth and critical-mineral flows, and AI.
key_facts.excerpt: The meetings at JP Morgan Chase's headquarters in Manhattan, which also will include US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, are due to start at about 10:30 a.m. (1430 GMT)... Key topics will be the status of a US-China trade truce that is set to expire on November 10, flows of Chinese rare-earth magnets and critical minerals.

key_facts.fact: At the close of the talks Bessent said the US had proposed a notification mechanism covering AI incidents that rise to a national security level, plus a new US-China AI dialogue, for the two leaders to consider.
key_facts.excerpt: Bessent told reporters that the two sides discussed setting up a new US-China AI dialogue, with a particular emphasis on national security concerns with a notification system for common goals and common threats that would cover AI-related incidents that rise to a national security level.

key_facts.fact: US officials said Washington and Beijing may be ready to ease tariffs on a narrow band of non-strategic goods, but that the US was not prepared to ease export controls in exchange for greater rare-earth flows; Trump will break protocol by greeting Xi at Joint Base Andrews.
key_facts.excerpt: US officials said Washington and Beijing may be ready to ease some tariffs on some nonstrategic goods... they said they did not expect the United States would be ready to ease export controls to allow for a greater flow of rare earth minerals... Trump will be there to welcome Xi for the state visit... That's unusual.

key_facts.fact: China's commerce ministry said the two sides are negotiating a reciprocal tariff-reduction framework covering $30 billion of products from each side; unfinished commitments from the May Beijing summit include $17 billion a year in extra US farm purchases and over 200 Boeing aircraft.
key_facts.excerpt: Beijing and Washington are also negotiating a reciprocal tariff reduction framework covering products worth USD 30 billion from each side. Chinese commerce ministry spokesperson Huang Ling said the consultations aim to reach such an arrangement at the earliest possible date.

key_facts.fact: The summit follows Trump signing the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which authorises tariffs of up to 100% on countries buying Russian oil and gas, including China and India.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump last week signed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which expands sanctions and gives the president powers to impose tariffs on countries that buy Russian energy.

stories.headline: FDA clears IntraBio's Aqneursa, the world's first drug for ataxia in ataxia-telangiectasia

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Aqneursa (levacetylleucine) oral suspension on Sept. 18, 2026 for ataxia in adult and pediatric patients with ataxia-telangiectasia weighing at least 15 kg — the first and only drug approved for A-T anywhere in the world, under Orphan Drug designation and Priority Review.
key_facts.excerpt: IntraBio Inc.... today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved AQNEURSA (levacetylleucine) for the treatment of ataxia in adult and pediatric patients with ataxia-telangiectasia (A-T) weighing ≥15 kg. AQNEURSA is the first and only drug approved for the treatment of A-T anywhere in the world.

key_facts.fact: The approval rests on IB1001-303, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial in 73 patients aged 4 to 50 across 10 sites in Germany, Slovakia, Spain, Switzerland, the UK and the US; 70 patients (96%) completed both 12-week periods.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval is supported by the pivotal IB1001-303 study (NCT06673056), a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial that enrolled 73 patients aged 4 to 50 years with genetically confirmed A-T across 10 clinical trial sites... Seventy patients (96%) completed the study.

key_facts.fact: On the primary endpoint the drug improved the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia by 1.9 points versus placebo (95% CI -2.7 to -1.1; p<0.001); the FDA's primary measure, the functional SARA, moved -0.6 points (95% CI -0.9 to -0.2; p<0.001).
key_facts.excerpt: AQNEURSA demonstrated statistically significant improvement compared to placebo on the primary efficacy endpoint, the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA) with a treatment difference of -1.9 points (95% CI: –2.7, –1.1; two-sided p<0.001)... Patients who received AQNEURSA showed a greater improvement in fSARA score, with a mean treatment difference of −0.6.

key_facts.fact: No treatment-related serious adverse events and no deaths occurred, and no patient discontinued because of a treatment-related adverse event; the most common reactions were falls and skin lacerations.
key_facts.excerpt: AQNEURSA was well tolerated. No treatment-related serious adverse events and no deaths occurred, and no patients discontinued because of a treatment-related adverse event. The most common adverse reactions... were fall and skin laceration.

key_facts.fact: This is levacetylleucine's second US indication after its September 2024 approval for neurological manifestations of Niemann-Pick disease type C; the label covers ataxia only, not A-T's immunodeficiency or elevated lymphoma risk, and there is still no cure.
key_facts.excerpt: This is a second U.S. indication, not a new molecular entity... FDA did not publish an overall-survival or cancer-risk result. A-T still causes immunodeficiency and a high lymphoma risk; this label covers ataxia, not those systemic features.

key_facts.fact: Results from the pivotal trial were published in the July 2026 issue of The Lancet Neurology.
key_facts.excerpt: These findings were published in the July 2026 issue of The Lancet Neurology.

stories.headline: Telix buys Germany's ITM for $1.65B to build a vertically integrated radiopharma group

key_facts.fact: Telix Pharmaceuticals announced on Sept. 21 (Melbourne time) that it signed an agreement to acquire 100% of ITM Isotope Technologies Munich for US$1.65 billion upfront on a cash-free/debt-free basis, with the investor call held at 7:30 p.m. EDT on Sunday, Sept. 20.
key_facts.excerpt: Telix will acquire 100% of the shares in ITM for US$1.65 billion upfront on a cash-free/debt-free basis... Investor conference call to be held today at 9:30 a.m. AEST Monday September 21, 2026. (7:30 p.m. EDT Sunday September 20, 2026 / 1:30 a.m. CEST Monday September 21, 2026).

key_facts.fact: ITM shareholders get about US$1.25 billion in 105.8 million Telix shares priced at US$11.84 (30-day trailing VWAP), released as Nasdaq ADRs after escrow; Telix also assumes US$302 million of net debt and owes up to US$700 million in milestones tied to ITM-11.
key_facts.excerpt: US$1.25 billion will be paid to the sellers in the form of 105.8 million Telix shares (priced at the 30-day trailing VWAP as of signing of US$ 11.84) and released to the sellers as Nasdaq-listed ADRs at the end of their respective escrow periods; US$302 million of net debt will be assumed by Telix at closing.

key_facts.fact: ITM, founded in 2004, is the only producer of globally scaled commercial-grade lutetium-177, distributes across more than 65 countries, and delivered US$273 million of revenue in 2025 after growing 40% a year since 2021.
key_facts.excerpt: ITM is the only producer of globally scaled commercial-grade 177Lu... Founded in 2004, ITM is a private company with a leading commercial scale radioisotope manufacturing and global distribution network spanning over 65 countries... delivered annual revenue of US$273 million in 2025.

key_facts.fact: The deal brings ITM-11 (lutetium-177-edotreotide), which completed a successful Phase 3 trial (COMPETE) in gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, with an interim analysis of a second Phase 3 (COMPOSE) expected in H1 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: ITM-11 (177Lu-edotreotide), a novel therapeutic candidate for the treatment of gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs), which has successfully completed Phase 3 development... fully enrolled a second indication expansion Phase 3 study (COMPOSE, NCT04919226) with an interim analysis expected in H1 2027.

key_facts.fact: Telix shareholders will hold roughly 76.3% of the combined company and ITM holders 23.7%; the merged group is projected to generate unaudited pro-forma 2026 revenue and income above US$1.3 billion, with closing targeted by end of 2026 subject to Telix shareholder and regulatory approval.
key_facts.excerpt: Telix and ITM expect to close the deal by the end of the year. The combined entity is projected to generate unaudited revenue and income topping $1.3 billion this year. Post-acquisition, Telix shareholders will own around 76.3% of the shares, while ITM backers will own around 23.7%.

key_facts.fact: Telix CEO Christian Behrenbruch said the merger 'positions Telix at the forefront of the consolidation that is occurring as the industry matures'.
key_facts.excerpt: Telix Managing Director and Group CEO, Dr. Christian Behrenbruch, said, "This merger positions Telix at the forefront of the consolidation that is occurring as the industry matures."

stories.headline: China runs six orbital launches in six days, closing with an in-orbit AI computing satellite

key_facts.fact: A Kinetica-1 Y18 rocket lifted off at 12:03 p.m. Beijing time on Sunday, Sept. 20, from the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone, placing nine satellites in their designated orbits and completing six Chinese orbital launches in under a week with a 100% success rate.
key_facts.excerpt: At 12:03 pm on Sunday, the Kinetica-1 Y18 rocket lifted off from the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone in Northwest China, sending nine satellites into their designated orbits... China completed six orbital launches in less than a week with a 100 percent success rate.

key_facts.fact: The streak began Sept. 15 and used six different vehicles — Zhuque-2E, Gravity-1, Long March-12, Kuaizhou-11, Long March-2D and Kinetica-1.
key_facts.excerpt: The mission capped a launch streak that began on September 15 and involved the Zhuque-2E, Gravity-1, Long March-12, Kuaizhou-11, Long March-2D and Kinetica-1 rockets.

key_facts.fact: One payload, Chaozhisuan-1, carries a four-metre visible-light camera plus an AI computer designed to process imagery and identify targets in orbit, cutting the need to downlink raw data; another, Pengcheng-1, is China's first demo satellite combining a 5G non-terrestrial-network base station and core network, onboard AI computing and a 100-Gbps space-to-ground laser link.
key_facts.excerpt: Among the payloads was Chaozhisuan-1, a remote-sensing satellite carrying a four-meter visible-light camera and an AI computer. It is designed to process imagery and identify targets directly in orbit... Another payload, Pengcheng-1... is China's first technology-demonstration satellite to integrate a 5G NTN... base station and core network, onboard AI computing, space-to-ground laser communications.

key_facts.fact: The Sept. 20 flight was the 16th for Kinetica-1 and the 68th Chinese launch of 2026; Chaozhisuan-1 is the third Chinese orbital-computing effort to reach space, after ADA Space and Zhejiang Lab's Three-Body Computing Constellation and July's Chenguang-1.
key_facts.excerpt: Today's launch was the 16th launch for Kinetica-1, and the 17th for CAS Space through its Kinetica family of launch vehicles. This was also the 68th launch from China in 2026... Chaozhisuan-1 is the orbital start of a third effort for space-based computing from China.

key_facts.fact: On Sept. 15-16 two privately developed rockets, LandSpace's Zhuque-2E and OrienSpace's sea-launched Gravity-1, deployed 18 Qianfan broadband satellites, bringing that megaconstellation to 256 satellites launched.
key_facts.excerpt: On September 15, a Zhuque-2E Y7 rocket developed by LandSpace sent 10 Qianfan satellites into orbit... Less than 16 hours later, the Gravity-1 Y3 rocket developed by OrienSpace launched another eight Qianfan satellites from waters off Shanghai. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology said the two missions brought the number of Qianfan satellites launched to 256.

key_facts.fact: For comparison, SpaceX flew its 107th Falcon 9 mission of 2026 on Sept. 19 from Vandenberg, the 81st Starlink flight of the year, on a booster making its 17th trip.
key_facts.excerpt: Saturday's launch was the 107th Falcon 9 mission of 2026, and the 81st of the year dedicated to building out the Starlink network... It was the 17th flight for this particular booster, which is designated 1093.
